definitions.explanation: The number of characters—kanji, kana, letters, and so on—in a piece of text. Most often used when there is a length limit, as in forms, essays, social media posts, and documents.

examples.japanese: {文字数|もじすう}を{数|かぞ}える。
examples.english: to count the number of characters.

examples.japanese: レポートには{文字数|もじすう}の{制限|せいげん}がある。
examples.english: The report has a character limit.

examples.japanese: ツイートは{文字数|もじすう}が{限|かぎ}られているので、{言|い}いたいことを{短|みじか}くまとめた。
examples.english: Tweets have a limited character count, so I summarized what I wanted to say briefly.

notes:
Combines {文字|もじ} (character, letter) + {数|すう} (number, count). Refers to how many characters a piece of text contains, usually in the context of a length limit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {文字数|もじすう}を{数|かぞ}える: to count the characters
- {文字数|もじすう}{制限|せいげん}: character limit
- {文字数|もじすう}が{多|おお}い: to have many characters (be long)
- {文字数|もじすう}をオーバーする: to exceed the character count
